q: Did games with smaller crowds coincide with smaller national TV audiences in 2025 and 2026?
title: MLB crowd size and national TV audience correlation, 2025-2026
cited: Yes, games with smaller crowds tended to have smaller national TV audiences, but a crowd that was small for its own park did not clearly mean a smaller audience (table: crowd_tv_headline). Comparing games on the same network, the two moved together (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62) (table: crowd_tv_headline). After comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, the link mostly disappears (0.16 in 2025, range -0.05 to 0.37; 0.14 in 2026, range -0.08 to 0.34; both ranges include zero) (table: crowd_tv_headline). Across team-seasons, teams with higher average home attendance also tended to have larger average national TV audiences (correlation 0.51, n = 56, range 0.29 to 0.68) (table: team_crowd_tv). This is consistent with team-level factors such as popularity and market size, but the data does not show that one causes the other.
report:
Yes, games with smaller crowds tended to have smaller national TV audiences, but a crowd that was small for its own park did not clearly mean a smaller audience[1]. Comparing games on the same network, the two moved together (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62)[1]. After comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, the link mostly disappears (0.16 in 2025, range -0.05 to 0.37; 0.14 in 2026, range -0.08 to 0.34; both ranges include zero)[1]. Across team-seasons, teams with higher average home attendance also tended to have larger average national TV audiences (correlation 0.51, n = 56, range 0.29 to 0.68)[2]. This is consistent with team-level factors such as popularity and market size, but the data does not show that one causes the other[2].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons. Nielsen changed its method on September 1, 2025, so 2025 and 2026 figures are not like-for-like.*

q: How did Tigers crowds change in 2025, and why?
title: Tigers attendance and factors, 2024 to 2025
cited: The Detroit Tigers averaged 29,796 fans a game in 2025, 21.9% above the 24,433 their prior two years of crowds, win rate, and market would predict, up 25.1% from 23,824 the season before (table: team_season_model). This growth represented a total home attendance increase of 555,147 fans to reach 2,413,442 fans (table: team_season_attendance), pushing their average ballpark fill rate from 58.99% of capacity in 2024 up by 13.5 percentage points to 72.53% of capacity (table: games_clean; query: Q4). These larger crowds coincided with an 87–75 regular season where the Tigers reached 59–34 by July 8 and clinched a second consecutive postseason berth ([2025 Detroit Tigers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Detroit_Tigers_season)). The attendance gains also coincided with key roster additions, including signing free agents Gleyber Torres and Jack Flaherty, and acquiring trade-deadline pitchers like Kyle Finnegan ([2025 Detroit Tigers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Detroit_Tigers_season)).
report: The Detroit Tigers averaged 29,796 fans a game in 2025, 21.9% above the 24,433 their prior two years of crowds, win rate, and market would predict, up 25.1% from 23,824 the season before[1]. This growth represented a total home attendance increase of 555,147 fans to reach 2,413,442 fans, pushing their average ballpark fill rate from 58.99% of capacity in 2024 up by 13.5 percentage points to 72.53% of capacity[2]. These larger crowds coincided with an 87–75 regular season where the Tigers reached 59–34 by July 8 and clinched a second consecutive postseason berth[3]. The attendance gains also coincided with key roster additions, including signing free agents Gleyber Torres and Jack Flaherty, and acquiring trade-deadline pitchers like Kyle Finnegan[3].

q: Compare the Cubs and White Sox on attendance and national TV audiences in 2025.
title: Cubs and White Sox attendance and TV, 2025
cited:
The Cubs dominated Chicago baseball in 2025, drawing 1,572,245 more fans than the White Sox and securing 15 national TV appearances while their crosstown rivals had none in the data (tables: team_season_model, team_tv_summary; query: Q6).

### Attendance
The Cubs averaged 37,259 fans a game in 2025, which was 320 fans above what their prior crowds, win rate, and market would predict, while the White Sox averaged 18,072 fans a game, which fell 1,548 fans below their prediction (table: team_season_model; query: Q4). This coincided with the Cubs drawing 19,187 more fans per game, totaling 3,017,983 fans at Wrigley Field compared to 1,445,738 fans for the White Sox (table: team_season_model; query: Q6, Q4). The Cubs drew 89.9% of capacity with a 92-70 record, while the 60-102 White Sox drew 45.0% of capacity (tables: team_season_model, games_clean; query: Q7).

### National TV Audiences
The Cubs' national TV schedule consisted of 10 single games, 5 Fox window games, and 2 special event games, while the White Sox had no national TV broadcasts in the 2025 data (table: team_tv_summary). The Cubs averaged 1,126,444 viewers for those single-game broadcasts (table: team_tv_summary). An average audience comparison between the two teams cannot be calculated (table: team_tv_summary).

The Cubs drew 89.9% of capacity with a 92-70 record, while the 60-102 White Sox drew 45.0% of capacity[3].

The Cubs averaged 1,126,444 viewers for those single-game broadcasts[5]. An average audience comparison between the two teams cannot be calculated[5].
